strengths: Pearl creates after the catch with suddenness and YAC violence.

strengths: Royal's best tape trait is YAC — once he clears the first tackle angle he has a second gear that pulls away from pursuit.
Royal's listed 5-11 / 200 looks real on film: thick lower half, stays on his feet through arm tackles, and finishes runs with contact balance.
Royal is used as a true weapon — split wide, slot, and in the screen/jet-touch game — not a one-alignment perimeter guy.
weaknesses: Highlight cuts emphasize space YAC more than full stems vs press; route polish and contested high-point sample need more all-22 before locking those claims.
easton-royal.comparison: Royal comps to Deebo Samuel — 5-11 / 6-0 thick WR mold; sudden after the catch, contact balance, and enough mass to punish tackle angles (size-matched; not a Florida-alum default).
easton-royal.schemeFit: Royal fits Faulkner as a boundary/slot hybrid built for manufactured touches and YAC after the catch.
easton-royal.staffNotes: FILM VERIFIED 2026-08-09 from Brother Martin junior + soph Hudl highlight reels (watched). Verified: open-field speed, contact balance, thick frame, multi-alignment/screen usage. NOT enough clean sample on contested high-points or full press-release tree in highlight cuts — do not oversell those. Flip-watch Texas commit. Comp size-matched Deebo; skipped On3 Percy Harvin Florida-alum default.
easton-royal.projection: Royal projects as a Year 1 package/special-teams WR (screens, manufactured touches), Year 2 rotation slot/flex, with Year 3 every-down starter ceiling as a physical YAC weapon — not a pure length X.
easton-royal.insiderNotes: Watched junior/soph Hudl. Royal wins with thick-frame YAC and contact balance; highlight package is space-heavy so contested-catch/route-tree claims stay conservative until more tape.
easton-royal.recruitingStory: Easton Royal is a 5-star WR · listed 5-11 / 200 · Brother Martin (New Orleans, LA) · Texas commit — Closing Class Flip Watch.

strengths: Tookes gets off the ball with a quick first step and natural leverage for a long 6-3.5 frame.
Tookes uses active hands (swim/rip) to shed and create negative plays behind the line.
Tookes pursues with a hot motor sideline-to-sideline and finishes with closing speed for 260.
Tookes shows bend/flexibility to threaten from 3-tech or kicked-out edge alignments.
weaknesses: Tookes can play too upright at contact and needs cleaner hand placement so he does not lunge through rushes.
zahmar-tookes.comparison: Tookes comps to Ed Oliver -- athletic interior DL with first-step burst and active hands in a long, explosive mold (Tookes listed 6-3.5 / 260 with room to grow into that family).
zahmar-tookes.schemeFit: Tookes fits White's front as a penetrating interior who can also flex to 5-tech in odd looks.
zahmar-tookes.staffNotes: Vault film desk verified 2026-08-05 from On3 Hudl embed. Comp size-matched within ~1-2" -- not a Florida-alum default.
zahmar-tookes.projection: Tookes projects as develop into the DL room, earn early rotation snaps as a disruptive 3-tech/4i, then compete for a starting interior role -- starter upside as a quick-twitch run-and-pass disruptor.
zahmar-tookes.insiderNotes: Tookes gets off the ball with a quick first step and natural leverage for a long frame. Active hands shed to create negative plays; hot motor pursues sideline-to-sideline with bend to threaten multiple alignments.
zahmar-tookes.recruitingStory: Zahmar Tookes is a 4-star DL | listed 6-3.5 / 260 | Brighton (Rochester, NY) | Florida 2027 commit.
